area: Runbook validator-contract consumer used raw task-card bytes instead of the sealed semantic digest
finding: The completion compiler and its validator both seal task-card contracts with semanticTaskCardDigest, which intentionally excludes lifecycle-only fields. The independent release reviewer independently hashed the entire card file. A normal lifecycle update therefore made every valid contract appear invalid, producing 247 invalid-validator-contract findings and their dependent unregistered findings.
expectedBehavior: All producer and consumer paths must resolve a validator contract through one shared semantic task-card digest implementation. Missing cards, semantic content changes, duplicate contracts, malformed IDs, and command mismatches must remain fail-closed.
evidenceOrRepro: On 2026-08-21 the 0341 completion report contained 247 validator contracts. All 247 matched the compiler semantic digest; none matched the release reviewer's raw SHA-256. Replacing the duplicated consumer algorithm with the shared semantic digest reduced invalid-validator-contract findings to zero while leaving actual not-proven requirements and Wave exits unresolved.
followUp: Keep the shared digest seam covered by lifecycle-only compatibility and semantic-content-drift rejection tests. Do not repair this class by weakening contract validation or by regenerating reports without fixing the consumer.
